name: Independent Safety Oversight
summary: A body that is independent of company leadership can delay or stop a training run or a release for safety reasons.
description: Leaders under commercial pressure decide when a model is safe enough. An independent body with the power to stop a release keeps that decision from depending only on them.

criteria.label: Independent Body
criteria.description: Most members are not company executives and have no large financial stake in the company.

criteria.label: Power to Stop
criteria.description: The body can delay or block a training run or a release.

criteria.label: Full Information
criteria.description: The body gets unredacted safety findings before each frontier release decision.

criteria.label: Public Record
criteria.description: The organization tells the public when the body delays a release or overrules leadership.

orgs.summary: OpenAI has an independent board committee that can delay or halt releases, under commitments to Delaware's attorney general. Its chair reported two delays without details.

events.title: Framework lets board reverse leadership safety decisions
events.summary: The Preparedness Framework (Beta) says leadership makes safety decisions, and the board of directors can review them, ask for information and reverse them.

quote.text: Where necessary, the BoD may reverse a decision and/or mandate a revised course of action

sources.title: Preparedness Framework (Beta)

events.title: Safety committee becomes independent with authority to delay
events.summary: The Safety and Security Committee, now without the CEO, becomes an independent board committee. It gets briefings on safety evaluations and, with the full board, the authority to delay a release.

quote.text: The Safety and Security Committee will be briefed by company leadership on safety evaluations for major model releases, and will, along with the full board, exercise oversight over model launches, including having the authority to delay a release until safety concerns are addressed.

sources.title: An update on our safety & security practices

events.title: Commits to attorney general on committee's halt power
events.summary: As conditions of the recapitalization, OpenAI committed to the Delaware and California attorneys general that the committee stays with the nonprofit and can require mitigations, up to halting a release.

quote.text: The Safety and Security Committee (SSC) will remain a committee of the OpenAI Foundation, and will continue its current role of providing governance over the safety and security practices of all of OpenAI, including OpenAI Group.

sources.title: Our structure
AG Jennings completes review of OpenAI recapitalization
Memorandum of Understanding between OpenAI and the California Attorney General

events.title: Committee chair says it formally delayed models twice
events.summary: Committee chair Zico Kolter said that so far the committee had formally requested a delay of models two times.

sources.title: The chair of OpenAI's safety and security committee said they've formally delayed its model releases.

events.title: Signs accord requiring independent board committee oversight
events.summary: OpenAI signed the White House accord. Signers agree to name an independent board committee that gets reports from control teams and auditors and makes sure that issues are fixed.

quote.text: Designate an independent committee of the board of directors to oversee and receive reports from the teams operating the controls and the internal and external auditors and evaluators, as well as to ensure any issues identified are remediated.

sources.title: White House Accord on Super Intelligence

independent-body.commitment: Nonprofit board committee with no executives; Delaware attorney general published its terms.

power-to-stop.commitment: Can require mitigations up to halting a release, per Delaware attorney general terms.

full-information.commitment: The chair gets safety information given to the company board.
full-information.missing: No rule requires unredacted findings before each release.

public-record.commitment: The chair said the committee formally requested two delays.
public-record.missing: No regular public record of delays.

orgs.summary: At Anthropic, an independent trust elects board members and must approve some risk reports. A board committee of two independent directors oversees model safety.

events.title: Creates independent trust that elects board members
events.summary: The Long-Term Benefit Trust has five financially disinterested members. It can select and remove a growing part of the board, but it does not decide on releases.

quote.text: The Trust is an independent body of five financially disinterested members with an authority to select and remove a portion of our Board that will grow over time (ultimately, a majority of our Board).

sources.title: The Long-Term Benefit Trust

events.title: Board and trust get capability reports before deployment
events.summary: Responsible Scaling Policy 2.0 says the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer decide. They share the decision and the Capability Report with the board and the trust before they move forward.

quote.text: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed with deployment, they will share their decision–as well as the underlying Capability Report, internal feedback, and any external feedback–with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 2.0

events.title: Board and trust must approve some risk reports
events.summary: Responsible Scaling Policy 3.0 requires board and trust approval of a Risk Report when marginal risk analysis plays a major role in a decision to move forward.

quote.text: In the event that marginal risk analysis (see previous section) plays a major role in a decision to move forward, explicit approval of the Risk Report by the Board and LTBT (rather than just the CEO and RSO) will be required.

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 3.0

events.title: Trust can request external review of risk reports
events.summary: Responsible Scaling Policy 3.2 says the company will do a public or private external review of a Risk Report when the trust asks for it.

quote.text: In addition, upon the LTBT’s request, we will conduct a public or private external review of our Risk Report or sections thereof, subject to the procedures outlined below.

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 3.2

events.title: Signs accord requiring independent board committee oversight
events.summary: Anthropic signed the White House accord. Signers agree to name an independent board committee that gets reports from control teams and auditors and makes sure that issues are fixed.

quote.text: Designate an independent committee of the board of directors to oversee and receive reports from the teams operating the controls and the internal and external auditors and evaluators, as well as to ensure any issues identified are remediated.

sources.title: White House Accord on Super Intelligence

events.title: Filing describes board safety and risk committee
events.summary: The amended IPO filing says that two independent directors form a board committee that oversees model safety and security risks. The filing does not give it a power to stop releases.

quote.text: Our safety and risk committee consists of two independent directors, currently Mr. Liddell and Dr. Narasimhan, with Dr. Narasimhan serving as Chairperson.

sources.title: Amendment No. 1 to Form S-1 Registration Statement

independent-body.commitment: Trust of five financially disinterested members; two-director independent safety committee, per SEC filing.

power-to-stop.commitment: Board and trust approve when marginal risk analysis plays a major role.
power-to-stop.missing: In other cases the CEO and RSO decide.

full-information.commitment: Board and trust receive Risk Reports and deployment decisions.
full-information.missing: No rule requires unredacted findings before each release.

public-record.missing: No commitment found to report delays to the public.

orgs.summary: Google's internal governance councils approve deployment safety cases. Google signed an accord to name an independent board committee for oversight.

events.title: Governance body must approve safety case before deployment
events.summary: Frontier Safety Framework 2.0 says general availability deployment waits until a corporate governance body finds the safety case adequate. The named bodies are internal councils.

quote.text: of a model takes place only after the appropriate corporate governance body determines the safety case regarding each CCL the model has reached to be adequate.

sources.title: Frontier Safety Framework, Version 2.0

events.title: Signs accord requiring independent board committee oversight
events.summary: Google signed the White House accord. Signers agree to name an independent board committee that gets reports from control teams and auditors and makes sure that issues are fixed.

quote.text: Designate an independent committee of the board of directors to oversee and receive reports from the teams operating the controls and the internal and external auditors and evaluators, as well as to ensure any issues identified are remediated.

sources.title: White House Accord on Super Intelligence

independent-body.commitment: Signed the accord to name an independent board committee.
independent-body.missing: No committee named yet; internal councils decide on releases.

power-to-stop.commitment: Internal councils must approve the safety case before general-availability deployment.
power-to-stop.missing: No independent body has power to stop a release.

full-information.commitment: The accord committee will get reports from control teams and auditors.
full-information.missing: No rule found on unredacted findings before each release.

public-record.missing: No commitment found to report delays to the public.

orgs.summary: Meta signed an accord to name an independent board committee, and says it will create an AI committee of its board.

events.title: Plans new AI committee of the board
events.summary: Meta says it will create an AI committee of its board to review framework changes and check that operations follow the framework.

quote.text: We will establish a new AI committee of our Board of Directors, which will review future changes to the Framework and independently ensure that our operations conform to the standards we’ve set.

sources.title: Developing Capable Models Responsibly

orgs.summary: At Microsoft, executive officers make the final deployment decision under general board oversight. No independent safety body found.

events.title: Joint board reviews frontier models before release
events.summary: Microsoft says a joint Microsoft-OpenAI Deployment Safety Board reviews frontier models before their first release when capability thresholds are reached.

quote.text: When it comes to frontier model deployment, Microsoft and OpenAI have together defined capability thresholds that act as a trigger to review models in advance of their first release or downstream deployment.

sources.title: Microsoft's AI Safety Policies

events.title: Reports say early GPT-4 test skipped board review
events.summary: A former OpenAI researcher said Microsoft tested an early GPT-4 version in Bing in India in 2022 without the joint board's approval. Microsoft first denied it, then confirmed the test.

quote.text: After more research, we found that Bing did run a small flight that mixed in results from an early version of the model which eventually became GPT-4.

sources.title: OpenAI Whistle-Blowers Describe Reckless and Secretive Culture

events.title: Framework gives final deployment decision to executives
events.summary: The Frontier Governance Framework says executive officers make the final deployment decision, under general board oversight and internal audit. It does not mention the joint review board.

quote.text: The Executive Officers (or their delegates) will make the final decision on whether to approve the recommendation for secure and trustworthy deployment.

sources.title: Frontier Governance Framework, Version 1

independent-body.commitment: Executive officers decide, under general board oversight.

power-to-stop.commitment: Executives approve or withhold deployment after internal review.
power-to-stop.missing: No independent body can delay or block a release.

full-information.missing: No statement found on which safety findings the board gets before release.

public-record.missing: No commitment found to report safety delays to the public.
